text: That heartbeat shakes the whole cleft, and the walkway behind them shears off the rock and falls into the dark.
The foreman, stranded on the far side, isn't paid for this. He's getting the engineers.
What's left of the walkway tilts, and Jaeha hauls Uncle Pyo up as his bad knee buckles.
At the low end, a narrow ladder runs straight down into the dark.
They're cut off, Moon Ahin observes, dusting off her coat. Then the only way is down, says Jaeha. And he has two more husks down there.
So she offers a truce. Until they're out.
Jaeha holds out his hand to shake on it.
She walks straight past it.
Down the ladder they go, eighty metres, Moon Ahin first, Jaeha last.
At the bottom is an ancient Far Side tunnel with the giant pipes humming along it. Dami ties a strip of her scarf round Jaeha's bleeding shoulder.
Then Borro heaves himself out of the black water, Lyra springs off his shell, and the crew scream. More husks! A huge one and a pretty one!
Lyra looks Moon Ahin up and down. Who wears white into a sewer? Says the woman wearing a belt as a skirt.
Jaeha sweats between them. Nib chews dried squid.
Nib scouts ahead, and Moon Ahin sends her lead husk, Number One, with him.
They walk side by side. Neither speaks.
They peek round the corner in exactly the same pose.
Behind them, she asks why he still calls them husks, after the whole country saw the stream. Because nobody tries to take a husk away from you.
And why do hers have numbers instead of names? Because she loses them. Uncle Taegun taught her that. You don't name what you lose.
Funny, Jaeha says. He names everything he doesn't want to lose.
For one instant, her composure cracks.
Behind them, Ho asks Borro if he's really a husk. I am Borro, says Borro.
Ho nods slowly. Cool.
Nib comes back. A pack of hounds, where the pipes split. Number One holds up fourteen fingers. Twelve and a big one, Nib corrects. Her husk can't count.
Number One turns its blank face down toward Nib.
In a round chamber ahead, twelve eyeless ash hounds lap at violet light leaking from a cracked pipe. In the middle lies their alpha, twice their size.
Jaeha's plan: her wall holds, his summons strike, and the pack only moves when the big one howls.
So her husks are the wall while his take the glory? No. Her husks are the wall because they're the best wall he's ever seen.
Then Ho sneezes.
The alpha rises and howls, and twelve hounds snap upright.
Moon Ahin's baton drops, and thirty-seven husks slam into a wall, Borro's shield in the middle.
The pack hits it at once. Three husks crack, but the wall holds.
Jaeha throws all three summons into field form. Carry still covers only two at a time.
Nib drops into the pack from above, and Lyra rains arrows from a pipe cradle.
One arrow misses. Moon Ahin doesn't even turn her head. You missed. Lyra was warming up!
Then the alpha leaps the wall and lands among the crew. Dami falls, and Uncle Pyo throws himself in front of her.
Pin its legs, Jaeha shouts. When it howls, it stands still. Moon Ahin calls four numbers. Take it.
Four husks lock its legs. A fifth, number seventeen, takes its jaws and shatters.
The alpha howls, frozen for one instant, and Borro slams his shield into its chest.
Jaeha passes the blow through his own body to Lyra, and his nose starts to bleed.
Her arrow leaves with the boom of Borro's blow behind it and punches clean through the alpha.
The rest of the pack flees whimpering.
Uncle Pyo is still standing with his arms spread in front of Dami. Ten years, and it's the first time he ever stood in front of anyone.
Moon Ahin kneels by the shattered husk, the silver seventeen on its neck, and touches its broken face.
Lyra points at Jaeha's nose. It's nothing, he says. Good shot.
But Moon Ahin sees the blood, and the scarf on his shoulder, and understands. He takes their wounds.
Her husks feel nothing. That's why they're perfect. His feel everything, he says. So someone has to carry it.
Deeper in, the air shimmers with heat, and the light turns deep violet.
It's not the pipes, Ho whispers. It's breathing. Woo knows.
The tunnel ends at a curved wall of glass thirty metres high. Behind the fog, a vast dark shape fills the space.
The fog clears for a moment on something rough and coral-red, then blooms white again, like breath on a window.
All three summons go tense, as if they recognize something.
Lyra goes pale. It smells like the sea. Why does it smell like the sea?
Moon Ahin walks alone to a brass plate at the base of the frame.
Kanghan's hexagon logo, and under it, a small crescent-moon seal.
Her grandfather's seal. He founded the core division.
Then her family knows what's behind this glass, Jaeha says quietly.
The vast shape is reflected in her eyes.
It breathes out, and the whole wall fogs white.
She presses a gloved hand to the glass. Grandfather... what did you build?
